context: Standard variable rates are usually set by lenders with Bank Rate in mind, but they don't move in step with it.
Fixed rates follow where lenders expect Bank Rate to go, not where it is today.
The same measure for homeowners, for comparison. The two series are weighted differently by the Bank, so the gap between them is not a like-for-like price difference.
Landlords in England and Northern Ireland pay this extra on each band of the price when they buy another property.
Landlords in Scotland pay this Additional Dwelling Supplement on the whole price of another property.
Savings rates tend to follow the Bank of England's base rate, though banks don't always pass changes on in full.
